item.title: Schizophrenia Impacts and Treatment Priorities: Results of An Externally-Led Patient-Focused Drug Development Meeting Survey
item.description:
Feld: Clinical Medicine Kategorie: Medical Informatics Score: 82 Autoren: Ilse S. Peterson, Ramaa Chitale, Theresa Frangiosa, Holly B. Krasa, Paulie VonEdWærd-Benjamin, Anita Fisher, Jessica T. Markowitz, Arun Nagendra Journal: Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science Veröffentlicht: 2026-07-23 Abstract: Abstract
Objective Using survey data gathered for an Externally-Led Patient-Focused Drug Development (EL-PFDD) meeting led by the schizophrenia community to inform the US Food and Drug Administration, this publication examines schizophrenia’s impacts on daily life, reasons for discontinuation of medication, and desired outcomes of future medications.
Methods An online, cross-sectional survey about schizophrenia’s impacts on daily life, treatment experiences, and desired outcomes of future medications was developed for adults with schizophrenia and caregivers of adults with schizophrenia who could not complete the survey. Patient advocacy organizations participating in the EL-PFDD meeting recruited respondents via email and social media between August 9, 2022 and September 26, 2022.
Results 282 survey responses from 96 people with schizophrenia and 186 caregiver proxies are reflected in this publication. Both respondent groups reported significant impacts of schizophrenia on aspects of daily living spanning work and education, relationships, responsibilities at home, and finances. For people with schizophrenia, the most frequently reported reason for discontinuing medications was weight gain (66% of 83 question respondents); for caregiver proxies, it was “feeling flat” (57% of 165 question respondents). Preventing delusions, preventing hallucinations, and enjoying daily activities received the highest average ratings as desired outcomes of future treatments from people with schizophrenia, whereas preventing delusions and making it easier to maintain relationships had the highest average ratings from caregiver proxies.
Conclusions As exploratory work on community treatment priorities, this research can inform patient-focused drug development endeavors by patients, advocates, industry, and regulators to address unmet needs in schizophrenia moving forward.
DOI: 10.1007/s43441-026-01001-2 ISSN: 2168-4790 Tag der Erhebung (OOIR): 2026-08-21
